newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Top Briton at U.N. to head Oxford college.
newsitem.headline: Top Briton at U.N. to head Oxford college.

text.p: Marrack Goulding, the United Nations undersecretary-general for political affairs, will leave his post to become head of St Antony's College, Oxford, sources at the U.N. said on Tuesday.

Goulding, 60, is the most senior Briton in the U.N. secretariat. Before heading the political affairs department under Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, he served as undersecretary-general for peacekeeping when Javier Perez de Cuellar held the world body's top post.
Goulding joined the United Nations in 1986 after a career with the British foreign service. He was ambassador to Angola from 1983 to 1985.
A graduate of Magdalen College, Oxford, he spent a term at St Antony's before joining the United Nations.
He takes up his new post in October 1997, succeeding Lord Dahrendorf as Warden of St Antony's, which specialises in post-graduate studies in international affairs.
